---
title: "Estimator bias"
execute:
  enabled: true
  echo: true
  warning: false
  message: false
---

Sampling variability describes how estimates change. **Estimator bias** asks whether their sampling-distribution center coincides with a named target:

$$
\operatorname{Bias}(T;\theta)=\mathbb{E}[T(\mathbf X)]-\theta.
$$

An estimator is unbiased for $\theta$ when this difference is zero.

## A target-specific comparison

We use the empirical mean adult-women /I/ duration in the Hillenbrand cohort as $\theta$. We compare the sample mean and sample median, both calculated from speaker-row resamples of the observed adult-women size. The median is not being judged as an estimator of the population median; it is deliberately being evaluated against the mean target.

```{r}
#| label: hillenbrand-estimator-bias
library(ggplot2)

vowels <- read.csv(
  "data/hillenbrand/vowels-complete.csv",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
women_hid <- subset(vowels, speaker_type == "woman" & vowel == "I")
x <- women_hid$duration_ms
theta <- mean(x)
n <- length(x)

set.seed(20261019)
replicates <- 20000L
draws <- replicate(replicates, sample(x, n, replace = TRUE), simplify = FALSE)
mean_estimates <- vapply(draws, mean, numeric(1))
median_estimates <- vapply(draws, median, numeric(1))

bias_table <- data.frame(
  estimator = c("Sample mean", "Sample median"),
  expected_estimate_ms = c(mean(mean_estimates), mean(median_estimates)),
  bias_ms = c(mean(mean_estimates), mean(median_estimates)) - theta
)

stopifnot(abs(bias_table$bias_ms[bias_table$estimator == "Sample mean"]) < 0.25)
bias_table
```

For the mean estimator, linearity of expectation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb{E}[\overline X]
&=\mathbb{E}\left[\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^nX_i\right]\\
&=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbb{E}[X_i]\\
&=\theta.
\end{aligned}
$$

The simulation estimates its bias at `r sprintf("%.3f", bias_table$bias_ms[1])` ms. The sample median's estimated bias for this *mean* target is `r sprintf("%.3f", bias_table$bias_ms[2])` ms.

```{r}
#| label: plot-hillenbrand-estimator-bias
#| fig-cap: "Sampling distributions of two estimators for the empirical mean. The vertical line is the named mean target."
bias_plot <- rbind(
  data.frame(estimator = "Sample mean", estimate_ms = mean_estimates),
  data.frame(estimator = "Sample median", estimate_ms = median_estimates)
)

ggplot(bias_plot, aes(estimate_ms)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), bins = 38,
                 fill = "grey75", color = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = theta, color = "#8B1A1A", linewidth = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~estimator, ncol = 1) +
  labs(x = "Estimate of mean /I/ duration (ms)", y = "Simulation density") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12)
```

A realized estimate can lie far from $\theta$ even when its estimator is unbiased. Conversely, an estimator may have nonzero bias but small spread. Bias is thus one property of an estimator, not a complete ranking.

## Check your understanding

1. Why is the sample median biased in this analysis without being generally defective?
2. What expectation appears in the definition of bias?
3. Distinguish realized estimation error from estimator bias.
4. Which target would make the sample median a more natural estimator?

<details class="understanding-answers">
<summary>Answers</summary>

1. The median is evaluated against the empirical mean, not against the median. Its bias is target-specific and does not make it a defective estimator in general. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->
2. Bias uses the sampling expectation $\mathbb{E}[T(\mathbf X)]$ and subtracts the named target $\theta$. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->
3. Realized error is $T(\mathbf x)-\theta$ for one sample; bias is $\mathbb{E}[T(\mathbf X)]-\theta$ across the sampling distribution. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->
4. For this empirical sampling reference, the natural target is the empirical median of adult-women /I/ durations in the observed Hillenbrand cohort; under a broader sampling model, it would be the corresponding population median. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->

</details>

The [mean-squared-error page](mean-squared-error.qmd) combines spread and bias in one target-specific criterion.
